A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 27-page versions of the same ACE study. Text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v2 reports original knowledge-editing experiments on GPT-J and Qwen3-8B, causal neuron interventions, ablations, and appendix robustness and locality evaluations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including multi-hop accuracy in Table 2, ablations in Tables 4–6, and counterfactual editing evaluations in Tables 18–19.

M1.justification: The attribution-based identification of query/value layers, sequential FFN edits, PMET optimization and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. The AlphaEdit extension also remains, with its appendix relabeled from J to K.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same MQuAKE subset, semantic categories, counterfactual scenarios and human-label alignment evaluation. Locality coverage remains CSQA, BBH, MMLU and GSM8k.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across corresponding experiments. FT, ROME, MEMIT and PMET remain in the main comparison; AlphaEdit already appears in v2 Table 10 and is retained in v3.

E3.justification: Subset construction, model sizes, edit counts, metrics, prompt configurations and optimization settings match. Experimental Settings and Prompts are relabeled from Appendices G/H to H/I without protocol revisions.

E4.justification: Layer and prompt ablations, neuron case studies, attribution robustness, intermediate-path masking and counterfactual analyses are retained. The knowledge-bottleneck sensitivity study moves unchanged from Section 6.5 to Appendix E, including Table 6.

E5.justification: Both retain the 1,000 sampling trials for the neuron-ablation case study and the same Pass@k attribution summaries in Table 13. No seed information, uncertainty-reporting practice or statistical test is added or revised.

E6.justification: All 19 tables and six figures retain their results. For example, Table 2 reports ACE averages of 46.45 for GPT-J and 58.24 for Qwen3-8B in both versions; Table 10 retains 49.24/61.54 for ACE with AlphaEdit.

T1.justification: The definitions, attribution equations and optimization derivations are unchanged. The formal logit-linearity, Taylor-approximation, additivity and PMET arguments move from Appendix M to N without mathematical revisions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about query-driven value activation, ACE's editing contribution, multi-hop performance and Qwen3's activation patterns.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations, architectural comparisons, semantic-interpretability discussion and robustness interpretations remain unchanged. The bottleneck explanation moves intact to Appendix E; no substantive qualification or limitation is added.

D1.justification: v3 adds an abstract statement that implementations are released and a direct GitHub repository link. v2 refers to supplementary code and future public release. Hyperparameters, prompts, hardware and latency documentation otherwise match.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix B and the reference list retain the same cited works and research positioning, including the relationships to IFMET and neuron-level attribution research.

P1.justification: Section 6.5 becomes Appendix E, subsequent appendix labels and cross-references are updated, and an acknowledgement and brief code-release sentence are added. The remaining prose is essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 6 moves into the appendix, and Figure 5 and several tables change placement through reflow. v3 also separates the Section 4.2 heading from the overlapping Takeaway 1 text on v2 page 5. Figure designs, table structures and captions remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves usability through the direct implementation link and correction of the Section 4.2 heading overlap. Moving the bottleneck study to Appendix E reduces its main-text prominence but preserves its evidence. Methods, results and theoretical support remain unchanged, so the improvement is limited to access documentation and presentation.
